newsitem.title: UK: LBMA to shed some light on opaque gold market.
newsitem.headline: LBMA to shed some light on opaque gold market.

text.p: The London Bullion Market Association (LBMA) intends to start publishing data reflecting the size of the traditionally opaque gold market, chairman Alan Baker said on Wednesday.
International settlement and London market turnover figures for the final quarter of 1996 will be issued next week, with the cooperation of the Bank of England.
Subsequently figures will be published monthly on a Reuters page, Baker said.
The LBMA represents the participants of the London-based wholesale gold bullion market.
The association was incorporated in 1987 in consultation with the Bank of England which was given formal responsibility for the market in the 1986 Financial Services Act.
The move was a response to calls from international markets for greater transparency in secrecy-cloaked bullion market, Baker said.
"Following many years of lack of information and data, the LBMA next week will be announcing statistics that will reflect the magnitude of the market," he said.
Greater transparency should not infringe on traditional customer privacy, he added.
"One is not giving away anything one shouldn't but at the same time one is trying to give some dimension to it," Baker said.
Details of the data to be released will be announced on January 29.
